title: A formal broker relationship can exist without verified consumer control
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office review of CMS controls over agents and brokers in federal health-insurance Marketplaces
geography: United States federal Marketplace; comparison with selected state-based Marketplaces in California, Georgia, and New Mexico

observations.period: 2024-2026; federal Marketplace agent and broker controls

denominator.unit: CMS federal Marketplace consent and access-control system reviewed by GAO

registration_control.value: agents and brokers must be licensed and registered; CMS restricts system access to registered agents and brokers

consent_control.value: consent processes were weak, access was not limited to the broker already associated with an enrollment, and consumers were not informed of all actions

2024_procedure.value: newer consent procedures were not always used and CMS took limited steps to confirm consumer identity

observations.method: GAO comparison of CMS controls with regulations and policies, review of CMS documentation, and interviews with CMS, stakeholders, agents, brokers, regulators, consumers, and three selected state Marketplaces.
observations.uncertainty: The control review does not estimate the share of all enrollments or plan changes that were unauthorized.
observations.subgroup: Consumers using agents or brokers in the federal Marketplace; agents and brokers registered with CMS.
observations.counterinterpretation: Registration and licensing remain useful safeguards, and stronger consent controls in selected state Marketplaces show that improvement is possible.

observations.period: 2023-2025; federal Marketplace confirmed unauthorized-enrollment and plan-switch complaints

denominator.unit: confirmed consumer complaints tied to unauthorized enrollments or plan switches

complaint_trend.value: grew more than fourfold from 2023 through 2025

likely_unauthorized_applications.value: at least 160,000 federal Marketplace applications in plan year 2024 had likely unauthorized changes

possible_consequence.value: consumers may be unaware of plan changes or lose coverage

observations.method: GAO review of CMS complaint and investigative information concerning unauthorized enrollments and plan changes.
observations.uncertainty: Confirmed complaints are not the prevalence of all unauthorized activity; likely unauthorized changes are an investigative estimate and do not show final resolution or coverage duration.
observations.subgroup: Federal Marketplace consumers affected by suspected unauthorized broker actions.
observations.counterinterpretation: The increase may partly reflect improved detection or reporting rather than a proportional increase in underlying activity; some changes may be corrected without lasting coverage loss.

denominator.unit: selected state-based Marketplaces reviewed by GAO

stronger_consent.value: selected states used controls beyond CMS, including one-time passcodes to verify consent for agent or broker actions

observations.method: GAO review and interviews concerning California, Georgia, and New Mexico state-based Marketplaces.
observations.uncertainty: The review does not establish that these controls eliminated unauthorized actions or produced better coverage continuity.
observations.subgroup: Consumers and brokers in selected state-based Marketplaces.
observations.counterinterpretation: State controls may have different costs, technical systems, or legal authorities and may not transfer directly to the federal Marketplace.

boundary: This record measures Marketplace broker controls, confirmed complaint trends, a reported estimate of likely unauthorized changes, and selected state safeguards. It does not establish national prevalence, final coverage loss, care disruption, financial harm, or post-correction trust.
